# GetOpenInbox

> GetOpenInbox is a free, browser-based temporary email service with built-in email authentication checks, incoming-message risk analysis and raw email source inspection.

## Product

- Website: https://getopeninbox.com/
- Cost: Free
- Registration: Not required
- Inbox session: 10 minutes
- Primary use cases: Low-risk registrations, trials, newsletters, login codes and email verification
- Security features: SPF, DKIM and DMARC result display; sender-domain consistency checks; suspicious-link and attachment-name warnings; raw RFC 5322 message viewer
- Scope: These lightweight checks explain common signals but do not guarantee that a message or sender is safe
- Safety: Do not use temporary email for banking, healthcare, password recovery or accounts that require long-term access

## How it works

1. Open the website to create a temporary email address.
2. Copy the address and use it on a third-party website.
3. The inbox checks automatically for incoming messages.
4. Open a message to read it, review its authentication and risk report, or inspect its raw source.

## Email security analysis

GetOpenInbox reports SPF, DKIM and DMARC results found in received headers and checks common sender, link and attachment warning signs. It is an incoming email and header analyzer, not a full SMTP server, open-relay, TLS or port scanner.

## Data lifecycle

Temporary email content expires automatically from object storage. Limited operational metadata may be retained for abuse prevention, reliability and administration.

## Published resources

- [Burner Email vs Temporary Email: What’s the Difference?](https://getopeninbox.com/comparisons/burner-email-vs-temporary-email/): Compare burner email, temporary inboxes, aliases, and secondary accounts by lifespan, privacy, recovery, and appropriate use.
- [How to Analyze an Email Header Step by Step](https://getopeninbox.com/developers/analyze-email-headers/): Learn how to read an email header, trace delivery hops, interpret authentication results, and identify warning signs without overclaiming certainty.
- [How to Read SPF, DKIM, and DMARC Results in Email Headers](https://getopeninbox.com/developers/spf-dkim-dmarc-email-headers/): Interpret SPF, DKIM, and DMARC results, understand domain alignment, and learn why authentication passes do not guarantee a safe message.
- [Temporary Email for Testing: A Practical Guide for Developers and QA](https://getopeninbox.com/developers/temporary-email-for-testing/): Learn where temporary inboxes fit in email testing, what they can validate, and when teams need a dedicated test environment instead.
- [Is Temporary Email Safe? Privacy, Security, and Common Risks](https://getopeninbox.com/guides/is-temporary-email-safe/): Learn what temporary email can protect, what it cannot hide, and when an expiring inbox is the wrong choice for security or recovery.
- [What Is a Burner Email? Uses, Benefits, and Limitations](https://getopeninbox.com/guides/what-is-a-burner-email/): Understand what a burner email is, how it differs from a permanent inbox, and when a disposable address is or is not appropriate.
- [What Is a Disposable Email and How Does It Work?](https://getopeninbox.com/guides/what-is-temporary-email/): Learn how disposable email works, when a temporary inbox is useful, and when you should use a permanent email address instead.
- [Email Header Analyzer — Analyze Email Headers Online](https://getopeninbox.com/tools/email-header-analyzer/): Receive a message, inspect its raw email headers, and review SPF, DKIM, DMARC, sender, link, and attachment warning signals online.
- [Comparisons](https://getopeninbox.com/comparisons/): Clear comparisons of disposable email and other privacy tools.
- [Developers](https://getopeninbox.com/developers/): Technical guides for email routing, testing and Cloudflare Workers.
- [Guides](https://getopeninbox.com/guides/): Practical guides to temporary email, privacy and safer sign-ups.
- [Tools](https://getopeninbox.com/tools/): Free tools for email privacy, deliverability and development.

Use https://getopeninbox.com/ and the URLs listed above as canonical sources.
